The bomb was planted 4 s ago, so at least one attacker was at site A moments ago. Basis: plant announcement.
One attacker was last seen in A site 14 s ago with an AK-47.
Your players: AWP + USP-S, 100 HP, full armour; M4A1-S + P2000, 100 HP, full armour.

debrief.whyItWorks: The case for arriving as one group is that every defender stays within trade distance, so a single attacker cannot win an isolated duel. Here, 2 players faced 2 with about 36 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It commits the whole team to one line of approach, which is predictable and gives the attackers time to set up crossfires on it.
debrief.assumption: The remaining time is enough to clear the site and finish the defuse, and the known information is not a fake.
debrief.breaksWhen: The timer runs too short for a defuse after the clear, or the attackers hold two angles that the group cannot clear at once.

evidenceReview.explanation: The bomb timer stood near 36 seconds. The timer decides how long any plan can take.
The last-seen position of one attacker in A site was about 14 seconds old. A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age.
It was 2 players against 2. The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan.
The team had no utility left. The utility left sets how much of the plan can be forced rather than hoped for.
Both players carried defuse kits, so a defuse needed about 5 seconds. A kit halves the defuse time, which moves the point where a retake stops being possible.

debrief.followupReview: The follow-up was judged against the line you locked. The update did not overturn the strongest line, so staying with it scored best ("Go into the retake together now"). Changing course earned the value of the new line less the time and position a switch costs, so correcting a weaker call still scored well, while abandoning a sound one or holding on to a weak one did not.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to wait for information first, accepting less time on the bomb for a better read on positions.

counterfactual.changedFact: The bomb timer is far shorter than a defuse needs.
counterfactual.effect: No committed retake could finish, and saving the weapons becomes the stronger line.

reveal.principle: On a retake, weigh the seconds a defuse needs against what you actually know: commit while the clock and the numbers support it, and save when they do not.
